_comment: Character registry. Adding a character is DATA, not code.
'parts' are SkinnedMeshRenderer prefab bundles; a part contributes every submesh it owns, so a
part that carries a head as its 2nd submesh (Tagilla) needs no separate head entry.

_animationsComment: A controller's m_AnimationClips are PPtrs that reach ACROSS bundles: TagillaBotAnimController
declares 847 clip slots but its own bundle carries only 430, the rest living in the shared
animation bundles. These are loaded into the SAME UnityPy environment as the controller so
those external references resolve; without them ~half of every blend tree reads as nameless.

_clipSetsComment: A clip set names STATES; the build expands each to every clip its blend trees reach.
Use FULL PATHS ('Base Layer.Stand.Idle_Aim'): leaf names like 'Idle_Aim' or 'MOVE' recur on
several layers, and a bare name resolves to whichever the walk reached first.
State paths are GRAPH-SPECIFIC -- the player controller and the bot controllers do not share
them -- so a character may override any set by name in its own 'clipSets'. Run --dump-states
to see a character's actual states before authoring one.

tagilla.note: Head mesh + Head_BOSS_Tagilla material are the 2nd submesh of the top prefab, which is why no head_boss_tagilla.bundle exists.
_equipmentComment: RIGID items parented to a rig bone. These prefabs are MeshFilter+MeshRenderer with zero
bindposes, and their `Dress` component lists only renderers -- the slot->bone mapping lives
in the runtime's PlayerBody.SlotView, not in the asset. So `bone` here is an AUTHORED choice,
not game-derived, and the manifest flags it. WHICH mask Tagilla wears is likewise a choice:
the bot loadout comes from the server's bot-generation templates, which are not captured.
'gorilla' and 'kill' (UBEY) are the two welding masks; head_tagillacap is his cap.
Paths beginning 'assets/' resolve from StreamingAssets/Windows, not the characters root.

glukhar.note: Complete outfit with NO equipment attachment: head_boss_glukhar carries his own headgear, unlike Tagilla whose look depends on a separate facecover item. Uses the generic bot graph.

pmc_bear.note: Clip sets not authored yet -- the player graph's state paths differ from the bot graphs'. Run --dump-states before using anything but 'all'.

scav.note: The everyman scav: bomber jacket + matching pants + a civilian head. Any other top_wild_*/pants_wild_* pair drops in the same way (outfit variety is data).
